Some phone makers have a SEPARATE battery/autostart manager beyond the button above — it only covers standard Android.
Confirmed on Samsung: Settings → Device care → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add Headphone Safety.

On Xiaomi/MIUI (not verified on this build — from dontkillmyapp.com): Settings → Apps → Headphone Safety → App permissions → enable "Background autostart," then also check Security app → Battery → App Battery Saver → Headphone Safety → "No restrictions."

On Huawei/EMUI (not verified on this build — from dontkillmyapp.com): Settings → Battery → App launch → Headphone Safety → set to "Manage manually" and enable all toggles; also Settings → Apps → Startup manager → allow Headphone Safety.

On OnePlus/OxygenOS (not verified on this build — from dontkillmyapp.com): Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → select "All apps" → Headphone Safety → "Don\'t optimize." OnePlus is known to periodically revert this setting on its own — worth rechecking occasionally.
On Oppo/Realme/ColorOS (not verified on this build — from dontkillmyapp.com): Settings → App info → Headphone Safety → enable "Allow Auto Start-up" and set Battery usage to "Run in background."

On Vivo/FuntouchOS (not verified on this build — from dontkillmyapp.com): Settings → More settings → Applications → Autostart → enable for Headphone Safety; also Settings → Battery → Battery Optimization → set to "Not optimized."
On other brands, look in Settings for a similarly-named "protected apps," "autostart manager," or "background usage" setting — see dontkillmyapp.com for a maker-by-maker guide.
More detail for any phone maker: dontkillmyapp.com
